title: Item
description: One catalogued file. Written only by the agent; the web module reads and never writes. The NAS is the source of truth and this document is a mirror of it — if the two disagree, the NAS is right and the next scan corrects the mirror.

id.description: Firestore document id. The content hash, so identical files across sources collapse to one document.

source.description: Which connector this item was catalogued from.

path.description: Connector-native id — for the NAS, the path relative to the share root. This is what an intent's item_id carries.

content_hash.description: The join key for every derived blob. Cheap fingerprint: file size plus a SHA-1 of the first and last 64 KB, so it never reads a whole file over the mount. Thumbnails live at 'thumbs/<hash>.webp'.

thumb.description: Blob key of the 400px WebP thumbnail, once pushed. Derivable from content_hash; stored explicitly so the UI can tell 'not yet generated' from 'generated'.

taken_at.description: Capture time from EXIF where available, falling back to mtime. What the UI sorts by.

latitude.description: From EXIF GPS, where present. Most photos have none — screenshots, edited exports, cameras with GPS off.

duration_seconds.description: Video length, where present. Best-effort within the same head-read budget as the rest of this item's EXIF — a video whose duration atom wasn't in that window (common for large, non-"fast start" files) comes back null, not an error.

indexed_at.description: When the agent last wrote this document.

state.description: 'trashed' means a delete action moved it to the NAS trash folder. The document stays so the deletion is visible and reversible.
